threads.body: This stable-semconv task is recorded under the same metadata condition as the legacy-semconv task. The metadata collector groups span files by this exact value, so it will merge legacy attributes such as `db.operation` with stable attributes such as `db.query.summary` and document them as one configuration. Include `otel.semconv-stability.opt-in=database` in `metadataConfig`, as is done when other test tasks enable multiple options.

replies.body:
Good catch, fixed in 1e4184a. `testQuerySanitizationDisabledStableSemconv` now records `otel.instrumentation.common.db.query-sanitization.enabled=false,otel.semconv-stability.opt-in=database`, so it no longer shares a metadata condition with the legacy task and the collector won't merge `db.statement` / `db.operation` with `db.query.text` / `db.query.summary` into one configuration.

I followed the comma-joined shape used by netty-4.0, netty-4.1 and jsp-2.3 for tasks that enable more than one option, keeping the same order as the `jvmArgs` above it. The semconv half matches this module's existing `testStableSemconv` value exactly, so the two stable tasks group together and apart from the legacy ones. All three values on the branch are now distinct.

Re-ran both tasks afterward and confirmed from the JUnit XML that each still selects only `InfluxDbQuerySanitizationDisabledTest` (1 test, 1 result file per task, no `InfluxDbClientTest`), and that the captured query text is still raw in both modes.
